title: Internal Hom
statement:
Fix the finite-field, scheme and coefficient data of [def-wf-weil-category]: $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in the chosen algebraic closure, a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $X_0$, and $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Put $R=\mathcal O_E$, choose its uniformizer $\varpi$, and use the completed coefficient sheaf $B=R_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(R/\varpi^n)_X$ on the small pro-etale site of the adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] for $A=R$ and $I=(\varpi)$; its hypotheses hold, since $R$ is Noetherian, $R/\varpi$ is a finite field of characteristic $\ell$, and each $R/\varpi^n$ is finite and has the length-one free resolution $R\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}R$. This is the coefficient sheaf on which [def-wf-weil-category] defines its coefficient category. All sites are small in the chosen module universe.

Let $D_{\mathrm{comp}}(B)\subseteq D(B)$ consist of objects whose completion map of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] is an isomorphism. Use the ambient convention
$$D(X,E)=D_{\mathrm{comp}}(B)[1/\varpi],$$
where the brackets mean raw scalar localization [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. Its bounded constructible subcategory is the coefficient category of [def-wf-weil-category]. For integral representatives $M,N$, use the ringed-site derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom],
$$H_B(M,N)=R\mathcal Hom_B(M,N)=Q_B\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(C,I),$$
where $C$ represents $M$, $N\to I$ is a K-injective replacement of a complex representing $N$, and $Q_B$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms. The replacement is taken among all $B$-module sheaves. Completeness here agrees with local derived $(\varpi)B$-completeness by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector]; [lem-sf-ringed-rhom-derived-complete] ensures $H_B(M,N)\in D_{\mathrm{comp}}(B)$ when $N$ is complete. Define $R\mathcal Hom_E$ on $D(X,E)$ by this construction on objects and by its bilinear scalar extension on morphisms:
$$R\mathcal Hom_E(a/\varpi^r,b/\varpi^s)=H_B(a,b)/\varpi^{r+s}.$$
Here $a:M'\to M$ and $b:N\to N'$ are integral morphisms; the displayed map goes from $R\mathcal Hom_E(M,N)$ to $R\mathcal Hom_E(M',N')$.

Write $\Phi_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(z\mapsto z^{1/q})$. Let $T$ be its exact module transport with the canonical completed coefficient identification $\Phi_X^{-1}B\cong B$ of [def-wf-automorphism-completed-transport]; its rationalized derived functor is the $\Phi_X^*$ of [def-wf-weil-category]. The derived transport preserves $D_{\mathrm{comp}}(B)$: the coefficient identification sends $\varpi$ to $\varpi$, so it carries the ideal $(\varpi)B$ to itself, and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-presentation-transport] shows that the local completeness tests of an object and of its transport are equivalent; by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector] these tests characterize $D_{\mathrm{comp}}(B)$. Hence $\Phi_X^*$ is defined on all of $D(X,E)$. Denote by
$$\alpha_{K,L}:\Phi_X^*R\mathcal Hom_E(K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_E(\Phi_X^*K,\Phi_X^*L)$$
the derived-internal-Hom comparison of the ringed-topos equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-presentation-transport], followed by scalar localization. Concretely, on integral representatives it is induced by $T\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(C,I)\cong\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(TC,TI)$, whose homogeneous components send a local map to its transported map; $TI$ is K-injective by the same cited equivalence statement.

For Weil complexes $(K,\varphi_K)$ and $(L,\varphi_L)$ of [def-wf-weil-category], define the internal-Hom Frobenius, in this ambient category, to be the composite
$$
\varphi_{R\mathcal Hom_E(K,L)}:
\Phi_X^*R\mathcal Hom_E(K,L)
\xrightarrow{\alpha_{K,L}}R\mathcal Hom_E(\Phi_X^*K,\Phi_X^*L)
\xrightarrow{R\mathcal Hom_E(\varphi_K^{-1},\varphi_L)}R\mathcal Hom_E(K,L).
$$
Thus the first argument uses $\varphi_K^{-1}:K\to\Phi_X^*K$ contravariantly and the second uses $\varphi_L:\Phi_X^*L\to L$ covariantly.

blueprint_update.statement:
On $D(X,E)$ the internal Hom
$R\operatorname{Hom}_E(-,-)$ is computed from a $K$-injective
replacement in its second variable. For Weil complexes the
internal-Hom Frobenius is the composite

$$
\Phi_X^*R\mathcal Hom_E(K,L)\stackrel{\sim}{\to}
R\mathcal Hom_E(\Phi_X^*K,\Phi_X^*L)
\xrightarrow{R\mathcal Hom_E(\varphi_K^{-1},\varphi_L)}
R\mathcal Hom_E(K,L).
$$

split_report.summary: Followed main-20261015 blueprint_update, replacing the duplicated conjugation wording by its typed composite. Made explicit the existing completed pro-etale coefficient model, ambient derived-complete rationalization, K-injective computation, bilinear action on localized morphisms, and the exact ringed-equivalence comparison. All constituent definitions and required well-definedness/completeness/transport facts already have DAG nodes; no new nodes. Finite etale-coefficient tagged Lean declarations do not give the same statement. Nine actual Mathlib searches, including a second semantic phrasing and corrected Loogle query, found no full match. reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q160-792cb3b50 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all of it: the item, the report, the master blueprint (order 2570) and the current blueprint (main-20261015, order 2914), unit sk-p-cyclotomic, the full statements of all nine cited nodes and of the related nodes (def-wf-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum, def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete, def-weil-pbc-rational-category, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-pur-integral-derived-operations, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit, lem-wf-internal-hom-weil), and Stacks algebraization.tex 099A (lines 930-935) and sites-cohomology.tex 08J7. The item matches the current blueprint: the internal Hom uses a K-injective replacement in the second variable, and the Frobenius is the composite of alpha with RHom_E(phi_K^{-1}, phi_L), with every arrow's source and target checked. Phi_X agrees with def-wf-weil-category. The bilinear extension to rational morphisms is well defined because H_B is O_E-bilinear. Completeness of H_B(M,N) follows from the reflector (b_1 = varpi) and from lem-sf-ringed-rhom-derived-complete (Stacks 099A). The comparison alpha follows from presentation-transport, which keeps the transported injective complex K-injective. Small cases checked: on Spec F_q with scalar Frobenii lambda and mu the datum acts by mu/lambda (inverse in the first variable), zero objects, identity Frobenius, shifts, the empty scheme. No new nodes, no duplicate found (def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom is consistent but only covers constructible pairs and has no Weil datum), no cycle, no SGA source, no tool_uses needed. Two small faults, repaired in the corrected item file. (1) E6/B3: the coefficient sheaf was cited from def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, but def-wf-weil-category, intrinsic completion, the transport node and the landed def-wf-tensor-product all use A_T of def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum, and no DAG node identifies the two sheaves. The statement now cites the adic datum with A = O_E, I = (varpi), its hypotheses checked inline, and stmt_deps swaps the dependency accordingly. (2) A gap: the statement did not say that the transport preserves D_comp(B), which Phi_X^* needs on the ambient D(X,E). I added that it does, by presentation-transport (c(varpi) = varpi) and the Koszul reflector, both already cited. Details are in review.md.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
